title: Lexicographically Smallest String After a Swap
statement: `s` is a string made only of digit characters. You may exchange two characters that sit next to each other in `s`, but only if their digits share a parity (both even, like `2` and `8`, or both odd, like `3` and `7`), and you may do this at most once, so leaving `s` unchanged is also allowed. Return the lexicographically smallest string you can end up with.
constraints: s contains only the digits 0 to 9
notes:
## Intuition

There are at most `n - 1` allowed swaps, so building each result and keeping the smallest works in O(n²). But a lexicographic comparison is decided at the first position where two strings differ, so only the leftmost spot that can be improved matters. A swap at `i` touches positions `i` and `i + 1` only, and it makes the string smaller exactly when the digits share a parity and `s[i] > s[i + 1]`. Taking the leftmost such `i` lowers that position and keeps everything before it; any other swap either changes nothing before `i`, raises an earlier character, or leaves the larger `s[i]` in place.

## Approach

1. Move `i` from left to right while a neighbour `s[i + 1]` exists.
2. Read the two digits as numbers `left` and `right`.
3. If `left % 2 === right % 2` and `left > right`, swapping them makes the string smaller: return the prefix before `i`, then `s[i + 1]`, then `s[i]`, then the rest.
4. If the loop finds no such pair, no swap can help, so return `s` unchanged.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "45320"`.
- `i = 0`: `left = 4`, `right = 5`: one is even and one is odd, so they cannot be swapped.
- `i = 1`: `left = 5`, `right = 3`: both odd and `5 > 3`, so return `"4" + "3" + "5" + "20" = "43520"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one scan, plus building one new string.
- Space: O(n) for the returned string.

## Pitfalls

- Only one swap is allowed: stop at the first improving pair instead of continuing like a sorting pass.
- Equal neighbours such as `"22"` must not end the scan; swapping them changes nothing (`"2231"` becomes `"2213"`).
- A falling pair with mixed parity cannot be swapped: `"21"` stays `"21"`.
- `0` is even, so `"20"` becomes `"02"`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i` | index of the left character of the pair being checked |
| `left`, `right` | the digits at `i` and `i + 1`, as numbers |

narration.2: Check each pair of neighbours from the left, because the leftmost improvement decides the order.
narration.3: Turn the left character into its digit value.
narration.4: Turn the right character into its digit value too.
narration.5: A swap is allowed only for equal parity, and it helps only if the left digit is larger.
narration.6: Swap this pair and return at once: no later swap can beat lowering this position.
narration.9: No pair could make the string smaller, so keep it as it is.
